note_bandwidth: copy measures read+write (2x traffic): true read BW ~8.4 GB/s single-thread. 48MB scan floor = 5.7ms. 2.8ms prediction needed 17GB/s: REFUTED quantitatively. 4-thread barely scales (controller saturated). DuckDB 6.4ms sits at the practical floor.
note_bounds: all variants within 11-15ms; zip SLOWEST. Bounds checks are NOT the 30-vs-8 gap cause (that was box load). Iterator-is-faster assumption also refuted.
note_fsync: fsync = 99.3% of durable cost (1.2ms vs 9.1us). Neither SQLite (2.1us) nor sheaf-db (6.9us) fsyncs per op. Our overhead is the per-op header rewrite (seek+write+seek-back); batch mode already 130ns.
note_amdahl: checksum total ~2% of 6.9us durable op. HW-CRC saves 109ns of 6900ns (1.6%). 100ns ring number is transport-only.
verdict: bandwidth floor CONFIRMED, fsync floor CONFIRMED (1.2ms), Amdahl CONFIRMED, bounds-check hypothesis REFUTED, thread-scaling assumption REFUTED (4t barely beats 1t).
